title: Bring back the focus ring that outline: none took away
summary: A blanket *:focus { outline: none } hid the ring on click, and on the keyboard too. :focus-visible shows it for the keyboard only.

turns.user: design asked me to kill the blue box that shows up when you click a button, so I did *:focus outline none. now QA says with the keyboard they have no idea where they are. what do i do

assistant.body: Got it. :focus-visible is the pseudo-class for exactly this. The browser decides from the last input whether focus should be shown. In other words, it does not match when a button is clicked with the mouse, and it does match when you Tab onto it. Current browsers already use :focus-visible in their default styles, so deleting the *:focus rule alone fixes the behavior. The default ring looks different in every browser, though, so replace the *:focus rule with this one to pin the color and width. The 2px outline-offset keeps a blue ring from melting into the blue button behind it.

turns.user: nice. but inputs still show it when i click them with the mouse? bug?

assistant.body: Not a bug, that is the spec. A text field expects you to type right after focusing it, so it matches :focus-visible even when you pick it with the mouse. The ring shows where your typing will land. Note: removing it here brings the original problem back, just on inputs. That is the reason to give design for keeping it on inputs.
